candidates.tagline: Apple's 'display' is 44% black bars — and Apple TV+ won't even run on it at launch
candidates.story: Apple launched the $299 HomeView smart display on October 13, 2026 with a 7-inch square screen (like an oversized Apple Watch) that shows widescreen 16:9 video in only 56% of the panel with black bars on all sides — and Apple's own Apple TV+ streaming service isn't available on it at launch.
candidates.why_funny: Apple built a product called a smart 'display' whose main use-case (video) fills less than 60% of the screen, then forgot to put their own streaming service on it.
candidates.alt: Apple HomeView smart displays in four colors — silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray — showing their rounded square screens mounted on white domed speaker bases

candidates.tagline: Tesla built a flying car. The flying part probably isn't street-legal anywhere.
candidates.story: Tesla unveiled its long-delayed Roadster on October 15, 2026 with SpaceX cold-gas thrusters that make it briefly fly and drive upside down — but a former FAA official warned the airborne features may require federal certification, production isn't until 2028, and customers who paid $50,000+ deposits in 2017 are still waiting.
candidates.why_funny: Tesla spent nine years promising a flying car, finally built one, and the punchline is that the flying part might not be legal to use — with production still two years away.
candidates.alt: White Tesla Roadster suspended in mid-air with cold-gas thrusters firing during the October 2026 reveal event at SpaceX's McGregor, Texas test facility
